(i) σ pp and ϱ pp go asymptotically like ln 2 s ; (ii) σ pp and σ p ¯ pp at the LHC and for cosmic rays can be accurately predicted; (iii) the cosmic ray measurements are not inconsistent with the predictions; (iv) σ p – air at the highest cosmic ray energies is not well determined, and (v) the Glauber model is a useful tool to connect the accelerator and cosmic ray data.
σ p p and ρ p p go asymptotically to a ln 2 s behavior at high energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of high-energy hadron scattering and the extrapolation of the resulting data to the highest energies.
the extrapolation of hadron–nucleon and hadron–nuclear cross sections to higher energies than have been measured.
the study of the hadronic interactions of high-energy cosmic rays and the Large Hadron Colliders (LHC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have a very good understanding of the hadronic interactions of the nucleons, pions and kaons at very high energies, and we are able to make very precise predictions of σ pp, σ π ± p and σ p – air, and of the ratio ρ pp, at energies far above those of present-day accelerator data

the LHC is expected to see σ pp ≳ 120 ± 10 mb and ρ pp ≳ 0.14 ± 0.02 at s = 14 TeV, while the cosmic ray measurements of σ p–air prod ≳ 500 mb at s ≃ 10 15 TeV, and ρ p–air ≳ 0, are not inconsistent with our extrapolations of the LHC data.
we have a robust and accurate theory of hadronic interactions, with the only remaining unknowns being the precise values of the parameters that characterize the theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Froissart-Martin bound is saturated at a value of 100 mb, and the ρ pp ratio goes to 1 at asymptotic energies, in accord with the predictions of Regge phenomenology.
the Froissart–Martin bound is indeed saturated, but that the saturation is not as rapid as ln s.

, in the absence of any new physics, we expect that the asymptotically free theory of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), which describes the strong nuclear interaction, will be able to predict σ pp, σ ¯ p ¯ p and ρ pp, ρ p ¢ p, at the LHC, and that the cosmic ray measurements will be in good agreement with these predictions.
